summary: Very recently, the BESIII Collaboration reported the first observation of a $J^P=1^-$ strange resonance in the $K\eta'$ system, the $K_1^*(1870)$. We examine whether this state can be accommodated in the kaon meson family. Although it cannot be assigned as a pure $3^3S_1$ or $2^3D_1$ state, we show that it can be described as the lower state of $3S$-$2D$ mixing, whose mass agrees with the measured value, and we predict its higher-mass partner. Using the quark pair creation model, we calculate the OZI-allowed decay properties of both \textcolor{black}{mixed} states; the total decay width of the lower state is consistent with the measured width of the $K_1^*(1870)$. We note that the subordinate $K\eta'$ decay mode of this state appears to contradict its observed $K\eta'$ decay channel, which calls for further study. We further investigate the production of these two states via the $Kp$ reaction, which may provide valuable information for future experimental searches.

title: Electromagnetic cross section of charmonium decay
summary: As an important measurable quantity, the electromagnetic cross sections of charmonium decay in an e+e- collider are valuated for fifteen final states. A general scheme of lS-coupling analysis is adopted for constructing covariant helicity-coupling amplitudes involving two-body decays with arbitrary integer spins. Based on the decay rate, the collision cross section is obtained finally. A number of illustrative examples is worked out to expound and incarnate the general formulas.

title: Charm quark energy loss fluctuations in clumpy color string medium
comment: 16 pages, 9 figures, submitted to International Journal of Modern Physics E
summary: We simulate charm quark propagation through an ensemble of color flux tubes formed between receding color charges in proton-proton collisions. Under the assumption of sharp string boundaries and a localized nature of the overlap regions, high flux tube densities lead to the formation of string clusters. We convert the local energy density of the superposed color field into an effective temperature of an ideal gluon gas and study the dependence of charm energy loss on its spatial inhomogeneities. By comparing different energy-density extraction prescriptions, we show that both elastic and inelastic momentum damping mechanisms are sensitive to the medium properties. However, the collisional channel is an order of magnitude smaller in absolute terms (up to $\sim0.15$~GeV) compared to the radiative loss (up to $\sim1.5$~GeV). Overall, the results demonstrate that the spatial overlap of individual strings generates a complex local energy density pattern, which predominantly governs the medium-induced quenching of charm quarks.

title: Quark + diquark description of nucleon gravitational form factors
summary: We present parameter-free predictions for the nucleon gravitational form factors (GFFs) using a Poincare-covariant quark+diquark Faddeev equation. We provide the full GFFs ($A$, $J$, $D$, and $\bar{c}$) along with their species decompositions into quark and gluon contributions. Based on the diquark breakdown, we find that while the scalar diquark component dominates the nucleon's energy, spin, and mechanical properties, the axial-vector component plays an indispensable role. The GFF $B(Q^2)$ is predicted to be vanishingly small but nonvanishing at finite $Q^2$; its physical origin is deeply rooted in the nucleon' s internal structure through cancellations in both the diquark content and the $u/d$ flavor sectors. Furthermore, our results for $\bar{c}(Q^2)$ confirm the fundamental symmetry requirements of the approach. Compared with lQCD, our calculated $D$-term and various spatial radii are somewhat smaller in magnitude. This systematic underestimation is primarily driven by the gluon sector and can be attributed to the omission of meson cloud effects, suggesting that these effects impact the gluon distribution more significantly than the quark distribution. Finally, our analysis of the energy density based on two extrapolation schemes reveals that the presence of a negative central energy density is highly model-dependent.

title: Exploring X17 Couplings through Meson Dalitz Decays
summary: The ATOMKI collaboration has reported anomalous $e^+e^-$ pair production in a series of nuclear transitions, which has been interpreted as a possible signature of a new light boson, X17. Meson Dalitz decays provide a complementary probe of the X17 interaction structure. However, the widely studied vector coupling scenario is in tension with the combined constraints from existing $D^{*0}\to D^0e^+e^-$, $D_s^{*+}\to D_s^+e^+e^-$ measurements and nuclear transition analyses. In this work, we investigate the X17 contributions to meson Dalitz decays within a framework incorporating both vector and axial-vector couplings, employing the Bethe--Salpeter approach to calculate the hadronic transition matrix elements. With $u$ and $d$ quark couplings taken from previous analyses, we identify allowed regions for the charm and strange quark couplings, which require the axial-vector coupling strength $|g_{c,s}^A|\sim10^{-3}$. We obtain four degenerate best-fit solutions, one of which is $(g_c^V,g_c^A,g_s^V,g_s^A)=(8.32,1.09,-2.62,1.36)\times10^{-3}$, and estimate the decay ratio $R^{\mathrm{th}}(D^{*+}\to D^+e^+e^-)$, which significantly exceeds the Standard Model prediction.

title: The Future Circular Collider as a photon-photon collider
comment: Proceedings of Science for the 43rd International Conference on High Energy Physics (ICHEP2026), 30 July - 5 August 2026, Natal, Brazil
summary: The CERN Future Circular Collider (FCC) offers a unique programme of photon-photon interactions in electron-positron, proton-proton, proton-lead, and lead-lead collisions, by exploiting the high-luminosity equivalent photon fluxes associated with the charged beams. Within the equivalent photon approximation, the electromagnetic fields of relativistic charged particles are described in terms of fluxes of quasireal photons. The complementary photon fluxes, energies, and virtualities available across the FCC operation modes provide access to a broad range of two-photon invariant masses and associated physics measurements. Physics opportunities open to study are highlighted, focusing on the exclusive production of C-even resonances, including the SM Higgs boson and searches for spin-0 axion-like (ALPs) and spin-2 graviton-like (GLPs) particles decaying back into photon pairs. These prospective studies demonstrate the potential to observe photon-fusion production of the Higgs boson for all colliding modes, as well as sensitivity to photon-coupled ALPs and GLPs with masses extending up to the kinematic reach of FCC-ee and into the multi-TeV range at FCC-hh collisions, with significant improvements over existing constraints.

title: HVP contributions to the muon anomalous magnetic moment in spacelike and timelike domains
summary: The hadronic vacuum polarization contributions to the muon anomalous magnetic moment $a^{\text{HVP}}_{\mu}$ in spacelike and timelike domains are recapped. The values of $a^{\text{HVP}}_{\mu}$ assessed within dispersively-improved perturbation theory are reported. The obtained results can be employed in the evaluations of $a^{\text{HVP}}_{\mu}$ in the framework of such methods as lattice studies, MUonE project, and others.

title: Strong Decays of the $2^-$ Heavy-Light Mesons in the Relativistic Bethe-Salpeter Approach
summary: We present a relativistic study of the mass spectra, the $^1D_2$--$^3D_2$ mixing angles, and the OZI-allowed two-body strong decays of the heavy-light $J^P=2^-$ mesons $D_2$, $D'_2$, $D_{s2}$, $D'_{s2}$, $\bar{B}_2$, $\bar{B}'_2$, $\bar{B}_{s2}$, and $\bar{B}'_{s2}$. The mass spectrum and the meson wave functions are obtained by solving the full instantaneous Bethe--Salpeter (Salpeter) equation, in which the wave-function representations are constructed directly in terms of the $J^P$ quantum numbers rather than the non-relativistic spectroscopic notation ${}^{2S+1}L_J$. For the decay amplitudes we use the partial conservation of the axial-vector current (PCAC) together with the low-energy theorem for the $H\to H'P$ channels, so that the light pseudoscalar meson enters only through its decay constant, and the effective chiral Lagrangian for the $H\to H'V$ channels. The total widths of these mesons are estimated by summing over the partial widths of all OZI-allowed strong decay channels.

title: Lean-Verified No-Go Theorems for $R$-Symmetries and Modular Symmetries in 4D GUTs
summary: $R$-symmetries are instrumental in supersymmetric model building. However, a no-go theorem restricts us from using them in a large class of four-dimensional (4D) grand unified theories (GUTs). Specifically, it has been shown that a supersymmetric 4D GUT based on SU(5), with finitely many chiral multiplets, cannot be broken spontaneously to the exact minimal supersymmetric standard model (MSSM) while preserving a discrete $\mathbb{Z}_M^R$, with $M \geq 3$, or continuous U(1) $R$-symmetry. We use Lean 4 to formalize this proof. In the process, we identify and close a gap in the general case of the published argument. Further, we discuss the implications for GUT models with modular symmetries. We point out that modular symmetries are inevitably $R$-symmetries in a supersymmetric framework that also describes gravity. At certain critical points in moduli space, discrete $R$-symmetries are linearly realized. In the context of 4D GUTs, the no-go theorem then implies that exotic states become massless at these points, provided the GUT-breaking vacuum preserves these symmetries. In the vicinity of these critical points, these exotics are parametrically light, which may spoil gauge coupling unification.

title: General Formulation of Covariant Tensor Amplitudes for Purely Hadronic and Single-photon Radiative Cascade Decays
summary:
We present a unified method for generating Lorentz-covariant partial-wave amplitudes for multi-body purely hadronic and single-photon radiative cascade decays within the covariant $L$-$S$ tensor formalism. Based on the structural decoupling of external polarization wave functions, complex coupling parameters, and the core covariant amplitude tensor $U$, we establish a hierarchical vertex contraction procedure that explicitly incorporates intermediate-state cascade bridge projection operators $P^{(J_i)}(p_i)$ and parent-frame definite-spin projection operators $P^{(S_{BC})}(p_A)$. This rigorous treatment guarantees the Rarita-Schwinger symmetry, tracelessness, and transversality conditions across different reference frames, fundamentally eliminating the unphysical longitudinal and trace contaminations induced by Lorentz boosts in cascade decays. Furthermore, we formulate a general covariant tensor representation for single-photon radiative decays $A(J_M) 	o \gamma + X(J_X)$ that strictly satisfies photon gauge invariance ($q^\lambda V_{\dots\lambda\dots} = 0$) in the Lorenz gauge. Built upon normal- and anomalous-parity fundamental transverse tensors ($K_{\mu
u}$ and $S_{\mu
u}$), universal recursive formulas are derived via the systematic replacement $g_{\mu
u} 	o q_\mu p_{A
u}$, accompanied by exact rules for matching the orbital angular momentum ranks of Blatt-Weisskopf centrifugal barrier factors $B_{L_{	ext{rad}}}$ and a spectator index pass-through mechanism for the photon polarization index.

title: Doubly strange tetraquark as a $KK^*$ virtual state: quark-model study with harmonic traps
summary: We extract hadron--hadron scattering information from quark-level interactions using an artificial harmonic trap and a four-quark basis that includes both meson--meson and compact diquark--antidiquark configurations. Combining the Busch--Englert--Rzażewski--Wilkens formula with the effective range expansion (ERE), we determine phase shifts, scattering lengths, effective ranges, and pole positions from the trapped spectrum. We control uncertainties from basis truncation, finite trap frequencies, truncation of ERE, and quark-model parameters. The extracted $DD^*$ and $BB^*$ binding energies agree with direct calculations, providing benchmarks. For the doubly strange $T_{ss}$ with $I(J^P)=0(1^+)$, we predict a $KK^*$ virtual-state pole about 30--35~MeV below threshold in the stable-$K^*$ approximation. Both the AL1 model and its modified version that better reproduces the measured $T_{cc}^+$ binding energy yield this result. This finding differs from earlier predictions of a bound state and motivates searches for the $T_{ss}$ at facilities such as the High Intensity heavy Ion Accelerator Facility (HIAF). This framework could be extended to other hadron-hadron channels to extract scattering observables and pole positions.

title: Colours and Flavours: ropes and colour reconnection as string multiplets
comment: 24 pages, submitted to the Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science
summary: The increase of strange-hadron yields with event activity and the enhanced charm-baryon fractions in hadronic collisions motivate a microscopic examination of how the colour environment affects hadronization. We review and develop the string description of these effects, starting from the Lund fragmentation baseline in electron--positron annihilation and following colour correlations beyond the leading-colour approximation. Few-parton examples show how junction formation and rope hadronization arise from the same SU(3) colour structure, connecting baryon formation and the screening forces that govern strange-quark production. For nuclear collisions, we introduce a local escape criterion and a phenomenological saturation of the breakup force, motivated by a three-string example of screening through background colour correlations. With common settings, the combined prescription gives a satisfactory description of light-flavour ratios in pp and p--Pb and provides O--O predictions. Charm ratios reveal a substantial remaining deficit in $\Xi_c$ production, motivating separate tests of the fragmentation baseline and its extrapolation with activity.

title: Dimension-seven spectator effects in charm-hadron lifetimes at NLO
comment: 41 pages, 8 figures, 8 tables; Wilson coefficients and diagram-by-diagram code as ancillary files
summary: We compute the next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD corrections to the connected current-current part of the dimension-seven spectator coefficients in the heavy-quark expansion of charm-hadron widths. The finite terms are fixed in NDR-$\overline{\rm MS}$, with the evanescent operators defined by the standard Greek projection and averaged over Hermitian-conjugate pairs, and with a finite subtraction that sets the finite mixing of the dimension-seven operators into the dimension-six ones to zero. In several channels the one-loop term is comparable to the LO coefficient, and two operator families absent at LO are generated. Since the NLO matrix elements of the dimension-seven operators are not known, we estimate the effect of the coefficients on the widths with tree-level matrix elements from vacuum insertion for $D$ mesons and from the bag model for charmed baryons. The $1/m_c$ corrections to the matrix elements of the dimension-six QCD operators are treated by a naive expansion. Without their $O(\alpha_s)$ part the semileptonic width of the $D_s^+$ would be negative. The NLO dimension-seven correction raises the $D^+$ width by 0.78 ps$^{-1}$, so that its central value, slightly negative as published, becomes positive. At central inputs, it is about 1% of the $D^0$ width, 10% of the $D_s^+$ width and at most 2% of the widths of the singly charmed baryons. Added to the published pole-scheme width, the $D^+$ correction gives $\tau(D^+)=1.41^{+\infty}_{-0.76}$ ps. The NLO term reduces the scale dependence of the nonleptonic dimension-seven contribution severalfold for the singly charmed baryons, whose matrix elements are evolved, but not uniformly for the $D$ mesons.

title: Muon and Tau Anomalies and $Δα_{had}^{(5)} (M_Z^2)$ in the Standard Model
comment: Latex sources, 19 pages, 3 Tables, 12 figures. Review talk given at QCD26(20-24 july 2026, Montpellier-FR) and at HEPMAD26 (26-31 october 2026, Antananarivo-MG)
summary: I review the present status of the Standard Model (SM) determination of the muon anomaly by emphasizing the estimate of the lowest hadronic vacuum polarization contributions using recent $e^+e^-$ data on $2\pi$ and $3\pi$ and the inclusive ratio $R^{ee}$ of total cross-sections compiled by PDG to which we add the QCD continuum including HO PT QCD up to $\alpha_s^5$, quark mass $m_q^2$ up to $\alpha_s^3$, $m_s^4$ up to $\alpha_s^2$ and QCD condensates. Adding the $e^+e^-\to \pi^0\gamma + \eta\gamma$ contributions to the CMD3 data, one obtains\,: $a_\mu\vert^{hvp}_{lo}=(7094\pm 37)\times 10^{-11}$. Combining this LO result with the HO estimate of the hadronic, QED and EW contributions, one obtains\,: $\Delta a_\mu^{sm} \equiv (a_\mu^{exp}-a_\mu^{sm})= (86\pm 38_{th}\pm 14.5_{exp})\times 10^{-11} $. The average of the recent estimates quoted in Table\,3 [$\oplus$ attempt to fit all $\,e^+e^-$ data] gives\,: $\Delta a_\mu^{sm} = (84.9[90.0]\pm 21.3_{th}\pm 14.5_{exp})\times 10^{-11}$\,. These results agree with the precise BMW20 lattice one and still suggest a window for new physics beyond the SM of $(2.1\sim 3.5)\,\sigma$. Besides some future projects for improving the $e^+e^-$ data, the MUonE for extracting directly $a_\mu^{tot}\vert^{hvp}_{lo}$ and J-PARC (E34) for an independent measurement of $a_\mu$, it is important to improve the Lattice results shown in Fig.\,9 which (at first sight) disagree each others despite the large errors and may question the reliability of the {\it averages of different averages} used in the White Paper (WP25) Our analysis is completed by updating the estimate of the hadronic contribution to the tau anomaly\,: $a_\tau\vert^{hvp}_{lo}=(3516\pm 25)\times 10^{-9}$ and to $\alpha(M_Z)\,: \,\Delta \alpha_{had}^{(5)} (M_Z^2)= (2770.7\pm 4.5)\times 10^{-5}. $

title: Longitudinal Parton Correlations in MRW-Type Unintegrated Double Parton Distributions
comment: 6 pages, contribution to the QCD at the Extremes 2026 proceedings. Summarizes results published in Eur. Phys. J. C 86 (2026) 1002; see arXiv:2605.15853
summary: Double parton scattering offers a way to investigate correlations between partons inside the proton that are absent from the usual product approximation for double parton distributions. In this contribution, we discuss how these correlations enter unintegrated double parton distributions when transverse momentum is generated using MRW-type prescriptions. Starting from non-factorized GS09 distributions evolved to unequal scales, we examine the double LO-MRW, virtuality-ordered MRW, and modified KMRW constructions, focusing on their transverse-momentum dependence and flavor structure.

title: Inferring the neutral-current neutrino--nucleon cross section from IceCube data
summary: Neutrinos interact only via the weak force, through the exchange of $W^{\pm}$ and $Z^{0}$ bosons in charged-current and neutral-current interactions, respectively. Recent experiments have measured the charged-current cross section at high energies, whereas neutral-current interactions remain largely unexplored experimentally. In this work, we investigate the sensitivity of the IceCube Neutrino Observatory to the neutral-current neutrino--nucleon cross section using 12 years of data. We consider two strategies to constrain this quantity: $(i)$ leveraging neutrino absorption and regeneration as neutrinos traverse the Earth; and $(ii)$ using the track-to-cascade event ratio. We find that current IceCube data can set only an upper limit on the neutral-current neutrino--nucleon cross section. We further show that IceCube-Gen2 should be able to constrain the neutral-current cross section with both methods considered here.

title: Cosmological Collider Signals from Fermion Bubble Loops with a Chemical Potential
summary: We present the first systematic analytical calculation of the local and nonlocal cosmological collider (CC) signals generated by massive fermion bubble loops in the presence of an effective chemical potential during inflation. Working in the de Sitter approximation, we investigate the four-point correlator of inflaton perturbations in the single-squeezed limit. By combining CC cutting rules, late-time expansions, and partial Mellin-Barnes (MB) techniques, we derive analytical expressions for both local and nonlocal signals. In particular, we identify two distinct contributions to the local signal, arising from spectrum and integer poles and from ultraviolet poles of the loop-momentum integral. We further investigate the three-point limit, where the separately extracted local and nonlocal contributions develop apparent folded singularities. By reorganizing the MB representation, we demonstrate that these singularities cancel in the complete signal and obtain a convergent double-MB integral suitable for numerical evaluation. Independent calculations using complementary MB representations provide nontrivial consistency checks of our results. We find that the chemical potential can significantly enhance the oscillatory signal while increasing its logarithmic oscillation frequency. Our analytical results provide a foundation for further studies of chemical-potential-enhanced fermionic CC signals, including fermion triangle loops.

title: A consistent (3D) EFT expansion of the bubble nucleation rate. Part I: scalar theories
summary: Precise predictions of bubble nucleation are essential for connecting cosmological phase transitions to their potential observational signatures. In this first paper of a two-part series, we develop a general, fully perturbative framework for incorporating higher-dimensional operators (HDOs) into nucleation calculations in scalar high-temperature effective field theories. Our approach consistently includes their effects on the bounce and the fluctuations around it, including interactions with higher derivatives. We prove that the resulting statistical rate is invariant under field redefinitions, and establish sufficient conditions for the existence of the perturbative bounce solution in the presence of HDOs. We illustrate the framework by applying it to a model containing a scalar and a fermion, where we find modest HDO corrections in its regime of moderately strong transitions. We thus extend the systematic study of HDO effects beyond critical thermodynamics and provide a controlled method for determining their impact on bubble nucleation.

title: Probing the QCD critical point through linearized sound wave dispersion and attenuation at finite baryon density
summary: We investigate the linearized sound-channel response of a finite baryon density Israel-Stewart hydrodynamic system coupled to a parameterized equation of state containing a critical end point. The attenuation of sound is characterized by a threshold wavelength below which sound perturbations are strongly damped. We systematically study the dependence of this threshold scale on the non-universal parameters of the Beam Energy Scan Theory (BEST) equation of state framework. In our present study, the threshold wavelength remains finite but develops a pronounced peak in the vicinity of the critical end point, indicating strong absorption of sound modes on fireball-scale wavelengths. We further estimate the impact of this enhanced attenuation on the linearized anisotropic flow response and find a reduction of the elliptic and triangular flow harmonics near the critical region. Our results establish a phenomenological connection between critical sound attenuation, Mach cone like correlations, and the linearized flow response in baryon rich QCD matter. These results suggest a non-monotonic beam-energy dependence of the sound attenuation scale. Together with a corresponding suppression of Mach cone like correlations and the linearized anisotropic flow response, they may provide a consistent signature that the system trajectory passes close to the critical point of the chosen equation of state.

title: Suppression, flow, and chemical components of heavy flavor hadrons in relativistic heavy-ion collisions within an improved Langevin framework
summary: We improve the Langevin model to incorporate both perturbative and non-perturbative interactions between heavy quarks and the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The transport coefficient of heavy quarks is evaluated by a potential scattering model in which both the short-range Yukawa interaction and the long-range string interaction are included. The updated model provides the correct thermal equilibrium limit of the heavy quark system with the medium background, and improves the accuracy in describing the nuclear modification factor and elliptic flow coefficient of $D$ mesons observed at RHIC and the LHC. Nuclear modification of different chemical components of charm hadrons, including $D^0$, $D_s^+$, $\Lambda_c^+$, $\Xi_c^0$, and $\Omega_c^0$, is investigated. Their spectrum ratios are found sensitive to not only the hadronization mechanism of charm quarks but also the medium-modified charm quark spectrum in heavy-ion collisions, offering additional constraints on the heavy quark dynamics inside a color-deconfined nuclear medium.

title: Phenomenology of neutrino mass ordering synergies in reactor, accelerator, and atmospheric neutrino experiments, and the role of the detector response
comment: 46 pages, 14 figures, 2 tables. Code available at this https URL
summary: The neutrino mass ordering is one of the main open questions of neutrino physics, addressed by reactor, accelerator, and atmospheric experiments and by their combination. When the data are fitted under the wrong ordering, each experiment returns its own value of $\Delta m^2_{31}$, its wrong-ordering solution. We show that this solution is a weighted average of the values preferred by the individual bins of the measured event spectra, in reconstructed energy and, for atmospheric neutrinos, also zenith angle, with weights set by their statistical precision. Both the values and the weights depend on the detector response. In the plane of $\Delta m^2_{31}$ fitted under the two orderings, the solutions lie on lines of slope close to $-1$, so that each experiment is described by one intercept. The weighted bin average extends the mass ordering sum rule to any oscillation experiment, including atmospheric neutrinos in Earth matter. It recovers the known closed forms for short-baseline reactors and for accelerators in vacuum, and for JUNO it equals a closed form evaluated at one effective energy, which depends on the energy resolution. Above the MSW resonance the frequency of atmospheric $\nu_\mu$ disappearance becomes nearly independent of $\delta_{CP}$, and the $\nu_\mu$ disappearance solution moves mainly with $\theta_{23}$. The atmospheric intercept depends on the energy and direction resolutions, the energy window, and the event classes, and differs between detectors. The synergy of two experiments is determined by the separation of their intercepts relative to their precisions on $|\Delta m^2_{31}|$. With JUNO, this separation depends strongly on $\delta_{CP}$ for an accelerator and is nearly independent of $\delta_{CP}$ and $\theta_{23}$ for IceCube DeepCore using all channels.

title: Mono-Z Signatures of Vector Dark Matter Detection at Future Electron-Positron Colliders: FCC-ee and ILC
summary: We investigate the mono-$Z$ signature of a vector dark matter (VDM) model at future electron-positron colliders. In this model, a stable vector boson, arising from an extended $U(1)$ gauge symmetry, serves as a viable DM candidate that interacts with the Standard Model (SM) through a Higgs portal. We perform a detailed cut-based analysis for the mono-$Z$ channel at the FCC-ee (with $\sqrt{s}=240$ and $365$ GeV) and the ILC (with $\sqrt{s}=1$ TeV), considering both leptonic and hadronic decays of the $Z$ boson. Signal significances are evaluated for benchmark points using fast event simulation with MadGraph5, PYTHIA8, and Delphes3. Our results demonstrate that future $e^+e^-$ colliders provide excellent sensitivity to Higgs-portal VDM, with the ILC's beam polarization offering an additional handle to suppress SM backgrounds. This study highlights the potential of lepton colliders in probing DM interactions.

title: Pulsar Timing Correlations Induced by Stochastic Spin-2 Ultralight Dark Matter
summary: Ultralight dark matter (ULDM) can generate time-dependent gravitational perturbations, providing a potential signal for pulsar timing arrays (PTAs). In Galactic halos, the velocity dispersion of ULDM gives rise to finite spatial coherence, which influences the correlations between pulsar timing signals. In this work, we derive the timing-residual cross-correlations induced by rapid metric oscillations of spin-2 ULDM, allowing for general polarization statistics. Under equipartition among the five polarization modes, the intrinsic angular kernel contains monopole and quadrupole components and exhibits an angular profile closely resembling that of spin-1 ULDM, suggesting a potential degeneracy between the two ULDM candidates in PTA observations.

title: Generalized transverse-momentum-dependent parton distributions of a photon and orbital angular momentum
summary: The coefficients of generalized transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (GTMDs) that encode the canonical fermion orbital angular momentum and spin--orbit correlation do not contribute to the direct transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) and generalized-parton-distribution (GPD) projections. We present, to our knowledge, the first explicit calculation of the leading-twist, time-even, chiral-even fermion GTMDs of an on-shell real photon at zero skewness and order $\alpha$. The coefficients $\mathcal{F}_A$ and $\mathcal{G}_A$, which multiply the $k_\perp\times\Delta_\perp$ structure, yield the fermion orbital angular momentum $\ell_z^f$ and spin--orbit correlation $\mathcal{C}_z^f$. For photon helicity $+1$, both are obtained in closed form in the leading fermion--antifermion sector and obey $\mathcal{C}_z^f=-\ell_z^f/2$ for a common transverse regulator independent of $x$, because the channel with the active fermion's spin anti-aligned with its orbital motion carries three times the integrated weight of the aligned channel. The projections reproduce the known photon TMDs and leading-logarithmic photon-to-fermion kernels, and energy-momentum-tensor overlaps reproduce the known one-loop photon gravitational form factors $F_1$, $F_2$, and $F_3$. Our result provides an analytic benchmark for fermionic orbital and spin--orbit structure in the real photon.

title: Inclusive Heavy Quarkonium Production in Lepton-Hadron Scattering in a Joint QCD+QED Factorization Approach
comment: 5 pages, 2 figures; contributed talk to HardProbes2026
summary: The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will provide an opportunity for precision studies of heavy quarkonium production in electron-proton ($ep$) and electron-nucleus ($eA$) collisions. Comparing production in $ep$ and $eA$ collisions provides a clean, well-controlled experimental environment to study interactions between a heavy quark pair and nuclear matter and the formation of quarkonia in a nuclear medium. In this talk, we present the first calculation of heavy quarkonium production in both $ep$ and $eA$ collisions at EIC energies using a joint QCD+QED factorization framework that treats collision-induced QCD and QED radiation on equal footing, and discuss the role of the nuclear medium in exploring how a physical quarkonium is emerged from a produced heavy quark pair. We also systematically extend our calculation to include next-to-leading power contributions in the inverse power expansion of quarkonium transverse momentum, and discuss the matching of our calculations to fixed-order calculations in the nonrelativistic Quantum Chromodynamics (NRQCD) approach.

title: Heavy double-gluon quarkonium and $\overline{b}ggc$ mesons
summary: We investigate heavy double-gluon hybrid mesons, built from a heavy quark-antiquark pair and two valence gluons, using the two-point QCD sum rule method. The charmonium-like $\bar{c}GGc$ and bottomonium-like $\bar{b}GGb$ states are considered with $J^{PC}=0^{\pm\pm}$ and $1^{\pm\pm}$, whereas the open-flavor $\bar{b}GGc$ states are classified by $J^{P}=0^{\pm}$ and $1^{\pm}$. The currents with $J^{PC}=0^{+-}, 0^{--}, 1^{++}$, and $1^{-+}$ vanish identically, so sum rules are derived for the remaining four channels. The operator product expansion is carried out up to dimension twelve, and the Borel parameter and continuum threshold are fixed so that the pole contribution dominates and the OPE converges. The resulting masses lie in the ranges $M\simeq 6.2$--$6.7$~GeV for $\bar{c}GGc$, $M\simeq 12.0$--$12.2$~GeV for $\bar{b}GGb$, and $M\simeq 9.2$--$9.6$~GeV for $\bar{b}GGc$, and the current couplings are obtained for all channels. These predictions provide a basis for analyzing the strong decays of double-gluon hybrids and for interpreting future experimental data in the heavy-quark sector.

title: Non-Canonical Q-balls in Polyattractor Inflation Models
summary: We show that Q-balls can exist in supergravity-based polyattractor inflation models that interpolate between $\alpha$-attractor T-models and polynomial attractor models. We consider both the original polyattractor potential and a natural generalisation. We find that Q-balls solutions exist when the model deviates significantly from the T-model $\alpha$-attractor, whereas in the T-model limit no Q-balls exist. These are non-canonical Q-balls due to the non-canonical kinetic term of the complex inflaton field. Such Q-balls could have significant cosmological consequences if they are produced at the end of inflation. In particular, if the global $\mathrm{U}(1)$ symmetry of the supergravity-based polyattractor model is unbroken, the Q-balls can be absolutely stable and could account for dark matter.

title: The Skyrme-Dilaton and Nucleon Observables
summary: We extend the Skyrme model by incorporating the $\sigma/f_0(500)$-meson as a dilaton. The motivation is twofold: the $\sigma$-meson is the lightest scalar resonance in QCD and is therefore the natural extensions to the pions of the classical Skyrme model, while its interpretation as a pseudo-Goldstone boson of spontaneously broken scale symmetry is supported by recent studies of gravitational form factors and related developments. Although the $\sigma$-meson is a broad resonance, for static observables it can be treated as real particle since its line-shape is not expected to be essential. A combined fit to static nucleon observables yields $\chi^2/\mathrm{dof} $ close to unity, with substantial improvement over the original Skyrme model, while simultaneously reproducing the physical value of $F_\pi$, the overall scale of the model.

title: Nonperturbative lattice simulation of the nucleation rate in thermal first-order phase transitions
summary: We present a nonperturbative lattice study of vacuum decay through bubble nucleation in a three-dimensional real scalar field theory at finite temperature. The vacuum decay rate is computed by combining an expanded-ensemble multicanonical hybrid Monte Carlo approach, which samples the critical bubble configurations, with real-time Langevin dynamics, which follows the subsequent bubble evolution. We extrapolate the nucleation rate to the continuum limit and compare it with the corresponding one-loop perturbative prediction, finding a discrepancy of about \(8\%\).

title: Non-Topological Chiral Anomaly: The Chiral Magnetoelectric Effect
summary: We derive the chiral anomaly in a thermal medium and show that, in addition to the well-established topological piece, the anomaly acquires a previously overlooked non-topological contribution, relevant for non-gauged axial symmetries. Remarkably, this modification of the continuity equation is independent of the electromagnetic fields, thereby giving rise to novel transport effects in relativistic hydrodynamics. We further propose an experimentally accessible new effect in Weyl semimetals which we call the Chiral Magnetoelectric Effect: an electric field proportional to the magnetic field is generated by the non-topological anomaly, even in the absence of an externally applied electric field. Beyond this concrete prediction, our results establish a broader hydrodynamic framework for non-topological chiral anomalies, opening the door to a range of previously unexplored anomaly-induced transport phenomena across condensed-matter and high-energy systems.

title: Spatiotemporal K-Shape: Reconstructing inhomogeneous condensate profiles on the lattice
summary: Spatially modulated chiral condensates can affect the phase structure of dense QCD effective models. Understanding such order requires characterizing its real-space structure as well as detecting a modulation. Spatial two-point correlators retain the ensemble-averaged power spectrum but discard relative Fourier phases, leaving the configuration shapes undetermined in general. We propose the Spatiotemporal K-Shape method to extract representative shapes from lattice Monte Carlo ensembles without assuming a functional form. The method extends K-Shape clustering to periodic lattice fields, aligning configurations modulo translations and, optionally, a global sign or phase before extracting cluster centroids. Comparisons across clusterings assess whether one representative shape suffices. Controlled tests recover distinct profiles with identical correlators and separate mixtures of different shapes. Applied to the $(1+1)$-dimensional Gross-Neveu model with $N_f=8$, the method extracts non-sinusoidal profiles with two sign changes at two chemical potentials and separates multiple shape families at a third, where a single centroid is insufficient. Including the discrete chiral sign symmetry in the alignment can fold domain-length fluctuations into an asymmetric centroid without implying a preferred ensemble asymmetry. The method thus complements correlator diagnostics with representative real-space shapes and information on their diversity. The application to the Gross-Neveu model provides a testing ground for configuration-based studies of inhomogeneous order relevant to the QCD phase diagram.

title: Confinement--Higgs Complementarity Viewed through Relative Quantum Reference Frames
summary: We formulate confinement--Higgs complementarity in terms of the relative orientation between two independently constructed quantum reference frames (QRFs): one derived from the gauge field and the other from the scalar field. Exact continuum and lattice identities give a relational interpretation of the scalar--color observables used in recent gauge-fixing-free $SU(2)$ simulations. In particular, we provide a QRF interpretation of the additional gauge-invariant nonlocal separation line obtained from the Cho--Duan--Ge (CDG) reduction reported in lattice simulations of the radially fixed fundamental $SU(2)$ gauge--scalar model. We explain why such a candidate nonlocal boundary is compatible with Fradkin--Shenker continuity and Osterwalder--Seiler analyticity for the appropriate class of local gauge-invariant observables. Separately, we show that a Wilson-rooted control observable admits an exact results at zero plaquette coupling and that it does not cause such a nonlocal separation line.

title: Fate of chiral and $U(1)_A$ symmetries in hot QCD matter under background magnetic fields
comment: 6 pages, 4 figures; Proceedings of the 22nd International Conference on QCD in Extreme Conditions (xQCD 2026), 14-17 July 2026, Busan, Korea
summary: We summarize our recent lattice QCD study of chiral and singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking in background magnetic fields. The magnetic field explicitly reduces the non-singlet flavor symmetry through the unequal light-quark electric charges. We therefore study two neutral-channel susceptibility differences: $\chi_{\pi^0}-\chi_\sigma$ for chiral symmetry breaking and $\chi_{\pi^0}-\chi_{\delta^0}$ for singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking. The calculation uses fixed-scale $(2+1)$-flavor HISQ ensembles with $m_l=m_s^{\mathrm{phys}}/10$, corresponding to a zero-field pion mass of $M_\pi\simeq220\,\mathrm{MeV}$. Magnetic fields enhance both susceptibility differences at low temperatures. Near the crossover, sufficiently strong fields instead suppress both differences. The suppression sets in at larger magnetic fields and is milder for the singlet-axial susceptibility difference than for the neutral chiral susceptibility difference.

title: On reflection positivity of lattice chiral fermions
summary: We point out that the overlap Weyl fermion, the spacetime lattice realization of a Weyl fermion underlying Lüscher's construction of lattice chiral gauge theories, is not reflection positive in two and four dimensions at finite lattice spacing. Consequently, the standard Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction does not yield a Hilbert space with a self-adjoint Hamiltonian. In two dimensions, we further show that the overlap Weyl fermion cannot be cut open: the lattice action becomes nonlocal in the presence of a boundary, as expected from the gravitational anomaly of the continuum field theory. By contrast, the overlap Dirac fermion is known to be reflection positive. However, its compact axial symmetry is not invariant under the reflection, whereas a reflection-invariant axial symmetry is noncompact, and both are part of an Onsager algebra.

title: Triple Exchange at the Cosmological Collider in Closed Form
summary: Particles with masses near the Hubble scale leave a characteristic pattern in the primordial bispectrum, turning inflation into a cosmological collider. For light fields, where this signal is largest, no closed form is known for the full shape of the quasi-single-field triple exchange. Using Feynman-integral methods, we obtain the first closed-form results, exact in the momenta, as expansions in terms of multiple polylogarithms around the massless and conformally coupled limits. We show that the template used in Planck analyses overestimates the amplitude by up to a factor of 1.8 and underestimates the mass, whereas our new template recovers both, as needed for current and upcoming CMB and galaxy surveys. We also compute the collapsed trispectrum and, combining it with the bispectrum, find that at weak mixing it bounds the self-coupling more tightly.

title: Global analysis of the $ρ$ resonance in lattice QCD
summary: We present a lattice-QCD study of the $\rho$ resonance in which we address the quark-mass and lattice-spacing dependence in a novel way using a global analysis of four $N_f=2+1$ ensembles. We parametrize discretization effects in the lattice energy levels and not in the scattering amplitude, which is defined in the continuum. We describe the amplitude using a $K$-matrix parameterization, which contains the light- and strange-quark mass dependence. By varying the parameterizations of quark-mass and lattice-spacing dependence, we examine the sensitivity of the physical-limit $\rho$ pole position to these choices and obtain the result $\sqrt{s}_\rho = 744(11)(7) - i\,69(7)(3)~\text{MeV}$ from a model average.

title: Thermal deep inelastic scattering, universality and complex geodesics
summary: In deep inelastic scattering (DIS), a lepton scatters off a target hadron whose structure is probed by an exchanged photon with large spacelike virtuality. We consider two-point functions of currents in strongly interacting quantum field theories at finite temperature in this kinematic regime and use a holographic description to compute them. At large virtuality, the crossover from vacuum-dominated to thermally dominated physics corresponds to a transition from exponentially suppressed absorption to power-law behavior of the response functions. This regime is related to a particular near-lightcone limit of thermal CFT correlators. We show that the response functions exhibit a large degree of universality: the dependence on the three-point couplings of currents to the stress tensor enters through a channel-dependent coefficient multiplying the kinematic parameter that controls the relative size of vacuum and thermal effects. The same coefficient controls conformal collider bounds; when either bound is saturated, the corresponding response function takes its vacuum form in the near-lightcone limit. Furthermore, the absorption exponent in the low-temperature regime is related to a complex geodesic propagating in the near-lightcone geometry.

title: Soft momentum expansion about the Stokes topological limit of Bogoliubov coefficients
summary: It is known that particle production in time-dependent cosmological backgrounds can be computed using the Stokes phenomena occurring in Bogoliubov transformations with an analytically continued time coordinate. We analytically compute the soft momentum expansion of the particle production amplitude about the Stokes topological limit that was recently discovered in this context. The computational technique relies on an exponentially improved asymptotic expansion that involves automorphisms in the space of functions defined partly by the angular step function intrinsic to the Stokes topological sectors. We combine this with special discrete symmetries tied to the time dependence of the dispersion relation $\omega_k^2(z) = C(k) + A z^n$ for even $n$ to explicitly compute the leading momentum dependence of the amplitude which is nonperturbative in $A$. We also use this result to give a semi-analytic estimate of the number density of particles in this class of scenarios.

title: Electric-magnetic asymmetry of exact dyonic Euler-Heisenberg black holes: duality-blind shadows and magnetically controlled horizons
summary: Maxwell theory is invariant under electric-magnetic rotations, and the Reissner-Nordström black hole depends on its charges only through the sum of their squares. The Euler-Heisenberg vacuum-polarization terms break this symmetry, and an exact dyonic Einstein-Euler-Heisenberg black hole was found recently. We ask which properties remember the breaking. Outside the photon sphere, almost none do. The metric function is even under charge exchange through first order in the coupling, the first odd term appears at second order and falls off as the tenth inverse power of the radius, and the shifts it causes in the shadow, the Lyapunov exponent, and the innermost stable circular orbit stay at a few parts per million. The core behaves differently. Any magnetic charge drives the metric function to negative infinity at the center and so forces a horizon, while an electric configuration lighter than its field energy can be horizonless. Whether an extremal limit exists is decided by one function of the charges, the maximum of the derivative of the mass function, whose critical curve reaches the origin along the electric axis and meets the magnetic axis at a closed-form value. Two independent integrations confirm every number, and the shadow is tested against the Event Horizon Telescope image of Sagittarius A*.

title: Transient Information in Moving-Mirror Quantum Correlations
summary: We study how a finite dynamical history remains encoded in a quantum field after a moving mirror returns to a common thermal trajectory. Two compact deformations of the Carlitz--Willey ray map are related by reversal of a control parameter and share the same asymptotic null line and Hawking temperature. The pairing induces an exact even--odd grading of the peeling field and Bogoliubov transformation. The complex continuum covariance retains the transient sign at first order, while the leading monochromatic quadratic response is even under reversal. Finite-bandwidth wave packets convert this distinction into signed interference with the thermal reference covariance. In linear response, the signed squared correlation is quartic in bandwidth for the selected right-moving packets and cubic for matched Rindler/Milne packets. The relative cross-covariance phase has a linear bandwidth dependence, with its leading coefficient maximized in magnitude by the flat window among normalized real symmetric windows. Finite-amplitude corrections introduce an additional linear bandwidth term in the squared Rindler/Milne response. The distinguishing packets sample the transient history in retarded time, while both trajectories share the same asymptotic Hawking temperature.

title: Kalb-Ramond black bounces: throat-blind shadows and throat-sensitive neutrinos
summary: Regularizing a black hole removes its singularity, but which observations could detect the regularized core? We address this question for a Simpson-Visser black bounce built on the power-law hairy black hole that a Lorentz-violating Kalb-Ramond background produces. Measured in the areal radius, the bounce leaves the metric function untouched and changes only the radial measure. This single fact sorts the observables into two classes. The shadow, the innermost stable orbit, orbital frequencies and gravitational redshifts are blind to the throat. The instability of the photon ring, the brightness of its subrings, the oscillation phase of neutrinos and the energy deposited by neutrino pair annihilation respond to it through one universal factor. We derive an exact law for the subring demagnification that holds for any metric function. We also show that the throat enters the weak-field neutrino phase and the light deflection with different weights, so that combined photon and neutrino lensing can separate the mass from the throat. Ray-traced polarized images of a turbulent thin disk confirm that the direct image hides the throat while the first subring reveals it. For neutrinos emitted near a stellar-mass compact object the throat reshapes the flavor survival pattern and enhances the annihilation energy deposition. Two independent computations reproduce each headline number.

title: Metric perturbations in Einstein-Hilbert gravity: An alternative perturbative formulation
summary: We derive the ordinary gauge-fixed quadratic operators of the four-dimensional Einstein--Hilbert action in exponential and inverse-metric-density variables on an arbitrary reference background. With a single nonlinear background-harmonic gauge transported through the exact field map, the density operator is the trace-reversed Lichnerowicz operator, while the exponential operator contains an additional algebraic Ricci-curvature term. This difference arises from the nonlinear transformation of the background tadpole and vanishes on Ricci-flat backgrounds; a cosmological-constant check gives the corresponding cancellation at Einstein saddles. The construction retains the exact determinant contribution and specifies the associated Faddeev--Popov operator. At the first interacting order on a flat background, we show that the two gauge-fixed cubic actions differ by a term proportional to the free field equation, and independently evaluate the same nonzero three-point coefficient in both variables, with its normalization matched to the Einstein-gravity interaction. An exact Schwarzschild configuration satisfies the same background-harmonic gauge and is stationary under unrestricted exterior variations of the gauge-fixed action. Its density and exponential reconstructions are checked together with the bulk and boundary terms; a separate radial variation illustrates the loss of an equation after imposing a restricted ansatz. These results provide an explicit comparison of established field coordinates at the classical and tree levels; quantum loop calculations additionally require a common measure, regulator and source prescription.

title: Optical Appearances and Multiple Lensed Rings of Self-Interacting Boson Stars with a Double-Well Potential
summary: As horizon-scale imaging opens a new era of strong-field gravity tests, self-interacting boson stars have emerged as compelling dark matter candidates and natural black hole mimickers. We systematically investigate the optical appearances and multiple lensed rings of such horizonless objects illuminated by a geometrically thin accretion disk. To overcome the severe numerical stiffness caused by the slowly decaying scalar tail, we introduce a robust hybrid metric reconstruction framework---seamlessly bridging an interior 6-parameter Padé approximant to the exact exterior Schwarzschild spacetime via a globally $C^2$-continuous cubic spline. This ensures high-precision ray-tracing across the entire domain. For the adopted double-well potential, we identify a strict upper bound ($\phi_0 \lesssim 0.317$) for the existence of regular static solutions. Crucially, we uncover a striking non-monotonic evolution in the shadow size, driven by a macroscopic mass-amplitude turnover that is fundamentally rooted in the microphysical competition between attractive and repulsive self-interactions. Within the most compact configurations, extreme gravitational lensing generates prominent nested higher-order photon rings and distinctly separated secondary images. Furthermore, exploring the scalar potential parameter space ($\Lambda, \Gamma$) reveals a distinct diagonal gradient in the shadow size. Our findings demonstrate that next-generation VLBI observations can move beyond merely identifying horizonless objects, offering a novel geometric avenue to directly probe the microphysical couplings of dark matter scalar fields.

title: Fourier Transform of the Scalar Propagator with Quantum Light-Cone Fluctuations
summary: We derive the Lorentzian Fourier transform of the Gaussian-smeared light-cone contribution to the scalar propagator in Krein-space quantization in terms of a Meijer $G$-function. We characterize its distributional structure, recover the massive propagator by adding the Bessel-function tail, and derive an exact expression for the massless one-loop bubble kernel using a position-space prescription.

title: Thermodynamics and interior structure of density-responsive regular black holes
comment: 25 pages, 12 figures, 4 tables, author's accepted manuscript, accepted for publication in Classical and Quantum Gravity
summary: This work studies regular black holes motivated by the scalar sector of density-responsive gravity (DRG). An algebraic prescription with phenomenological local running maps a Gaussian matter profile to a diagnostic density profile. A pressure check shows that this profile does not solve the full static DRG equations. It serves only to select an effective metric family with two horizons. The extremal mass is calibrated to $M_{\min} = \sqrt{1+A/2}\,M_{\mathrm{P}} \simeq 1.006\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$, where $A=0.024$ is the historical scalar response amplitude. A fit to $\rho(r) = \rho_0\exp[-(r/r_c)^n]$ selects $n=2$. The temperature is nonmonotonic, reaching $T_H^{\max}=0.02547\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$ at $M=1.332\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$ before vanishing at $M_{\min}$. The calculation verifies the generic scaling near extremality $\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{tr}}\propto(M-M_{\min})^{-1/2}$ of a static lapse diagnostic for $n=2,3,4,6$ and for the Hayward and Bardeen controls. A regulated integral of coordinate time between the horizons provides a static cavity diagnostic, not a prediction of echoes of gravitational waves. The remaining area entropy equals the area entropy already lost at $M_{\mathrm{cross}}/M_0=0.707107\simeq1/\sqrt{2}$. This geometric crossing does not establish a Page curve or unitarity. The endpoint area entropy is below $2.6\%$ of the initial Bekenstein-Hawking entropy for $M_0 = 5\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$ and below $0.03\%$ for $M_0 = 50\,M_{\mathrm{P}}$. An inverse source reconstruction confirms an isotropic core of de Sitter type but retains the pressure mismatch. An exploratory collapse calculation with an imposed bounce factor produces bounded configurations with $1-2m/r<0$ without establishing formation of the calibrated geometry. The robust results are the calibrated thermodynamics and generic scaling near extremality.

title: Finite Energy, Event Horizons, and a Universal Bound on the Singularity Order in Born--Infeld-type Black Holes
summary: We investigate an interpolated Maxwell--Born--Infeld theory bridging the Maxwell and Born--Infeld limits. In the electrostatic sector the total energy is finite, and remains bounded above even as the theory approaches the Maxwell limit. We construct the electrically charged black hole, whose black hole solution interpolates monotonically between the classical Born--Infeld and Reissner--Nordström solutions; singularity can be relegated, independently of the weight parameters. For general interpolated theories with a truncation threshold, we analyze the existence and multiplicity of event horizons and classify the horizon configurations, and for general Born--Infeld-type nonlinear structures we prove a universal lower bound on the order of the Kretschmann divergence, thereby excluding regular electric black holes.

title: Resonance Induced Chaos of Charged Particles Around a Magnetized, Periodically Time-Conformal Reissner-Nordstrom Black Hole with Quintessence
summary: Astrophysical black holes are never strictly static: accretion, mergers, and gravitational radiation drive a slow evolution of their geometry. We model this evolution through a periodic time-conformal deformation, $\Omega(t)=1+\epsilon\sin(\omega_d t)$, of a Reissner--Nordström black hole surrounded by quintessence, and study the resulting onset of chaos for charged test particles. The deformation converts the integrable static spacetime into a periodically driven nonlinear Hamiltonian system, so that the transition from regular to chaotic motion can be related to the breakdown of an approximate Noether symmetry. The resulting two-degree-of-freedom Hamiltonian system is solved using an adaptive high-order Runge--Kutta integrator, while the dynamical behaviour is analysed through Poincaré sections, bifurcation diagrams, the largest Lyapunov exponent, and the Smaller Alignment Index (SALI). Our results show that the onset of chaos is controlled primarily by nonlinear resonance rather than by the magnitude of any individual parameter. Chaos grows with the conformal amplitude $\epsilon$ through resonance overlap, while the magnetic field $B$ acts non-monotonically: it produces chaos near the field strength at which the radial frequency matches the drive, and suppresses it at stronger fields by detuning. The small-divisor structure of the approximate Noether symmetry predicts the magnetic threshold without free parameters ($B_c\simeq0.011$ against the measured $0.012$), and reproduces the conformal threshold once a single coupling constant is fixed. In contrast, the quintessence parameter mainly facilitates particle escape by reducing the confining potential barrier, providing a distinct non-resonant route to the breakdown of regular motion.

title: Holographic Einstein rings of a covariant quantum corrected AdS black hole
summary: We investigate holographic Einstein rings in a covariant quantum corrected Schwarzschild--AdS$_4$ spacetime using a massless scalar probe. At fixed horizon radius $r_h$, the deformation parameter $\zeta$ leaves the metric mass parameter, coordinate surface gravity, and photon sphere radius unchanged, while increasing the photon potential maximum and the asymptotic lapse coefficient $A=1+\zeta^2$. The critical coordinate impact parameter approaches $A^{-1/2}$ for large black holes, whereas the corresponding incidence angle in the normalized boundary frame approaches $\pi/2$. Ray tracing and local WKB barrier data recover the same geometric scale. Quasinormal spectra computed with AdS boundary conditions provide a comparison at finite multipole number. These results separate the finite radius effect of the deformation from the change in boundary time normalization.

title: Polarized equatorial emission around regular compact objects
summary: We study the polarization properties of regular compact objects motivated by quantum gravity. These geometries include static spherically symmetric non-singular black holes which undergo a continuous transition to regular particle-like spacetimes in certain regions of the parametric space. Applying a phenomenological model of a magnetized fluid ring orbiting in the equatorial plane, we search for characteristic signatures in the direct polarized images which could distinguish them from black holes in general relativity. At low inclinations the regular compact objects lead to a very similar polarization pattern as the Schwarzschild black hole. At high inclinations we observe a characteristic signature for the particle-like geometries. A second direct image of the fluid ring is formed which is absent for black holes. It may possess with three orders of magnitude higher polarization intensity and a specific polarization direction making it observationally significant. We elucidate the physical mechanism for the formation of the second direct image and pinpoint the plasma configurations which lead to amplification of its polarized emission.

title: Landauer erasure and horizon information in an expanding universe
comment: 12 pages, 3 figures, to appear in EPL
summary: We investigate the thermodynamic cost of information erasure in Friedmann--Robertson--Walker cosmology by combining Landauer's principle with the thermodynamics of the apparent horizon. Adopting the apparent-horizon temperature as an effective cosmological temperature, we find that for standard non-phantom expansion, the minimum heat required to erase one bit decreases while the entropy-equivalent information content of the horizon increases. We further compare the Landauer heat with the Misner--Sharp energy and show that, despite their simple thermodynamic relation, they have distinct physical meanings. These results provide a simple connection between information erasure, horizon thermodynamics, and gravitational energy in an expanding universe.

title: Primordial Non-Gaussianity and Correlation-Function Perturbativity in mLQC-I: The Hybrid Approach
summary: We investigate primordial non-Gaussianity and the perturbative consistency of scalar perturbations in modified loop quantum cosmology I (mLQC-I) within the hybrid approach. We construct the cubic interaction Hamiltonian in the canonical representation of the quadratic theory and derive an exact finite-momentum in-in expression for the tree-level bispectrum. We consider two initial-state prescriptions: a Gaussian state specified at the bounce and the de Sitter vacuum specified at a remote contracting surface. We assess the retained nonlinear-conversion correction through $\Xi=|\Delta P_R/P_R^{(0)}|$. For the bounce state, a conservative, cancellation-independent, finite-window absolute-integrand estimate is below $6\times10^{-6}$ at all five sampled momenta. For the remote de Sitter state, the signed correction is dominated by cancellations and decreases from $\Xi\simeq9.9\times10^{-2}$ at one tenth of the bounce-curvature scale to $\Xi\simeq2.3\times10^{-4}$ at that scale. Although the retained two-point corrections remain below unity, the bispectrum can have large pointwise amplitudes: the bounce state yields an equilateral $f_{\rm NL}$ with root-mean-square amplitude over oscillation phase of order $10^3$--$10^4$, while the remote state can yield much larger values. The dominant rapid oscillation is organized approximately by $k_t=k_1+k_2+k_3$, with $\Delta k_t\simeq5.7\times10^{-4}m_{\rm P}$, while the triangle-shape envelope varies slowly. For the illustrative bounce-to-present mapping adopted here, CMB-projection diagnostics indicate substantial phase averaging. Thus, large pointwise primordial non-Gaussianity can coexist with a small retained correction to the two-point function.

title: Asymptotic stability of axisymmetric perturbations of near-horizon extremal Kerr with a Schwarzian-deformed throat
summary: We study the asymptotic stability of axisymmetric gravitational perturbations of the near-horizon geometries of (near-)extremal Kerr black holes and consider the family of backgrounds in which the AdS$_{2}$ factor of NHEK is deformed by a Schwarzian mode. Requiring the Killing parameter to be local in the background makes the Gelfand--Dikii polynomials natural solutions of the Killing equation, and that locality requirement brings stationary solutions of the Korteweg-de Vries equation. The hierarchy selects a family of backgrounds, which remain $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})\times \mathfrak{u}(1)$ throughout them: the first level gives NHEK and near-NHEK, the second, solitons that depart from one of these geometries and return to it. We linearize Einstein's equations around this family, where the axisymmetric sector reduces to a wave equation on the nearly-AdS$_{2}$ base, and analyze this equation by energy and virial methods. For NHEK we obtain a conserved energy, an integrated local energy estimate and asymptotic stability in a weighted norm; for a nonconstant Schwarzian the energy becomes a Lyapunov functional whose monotonicity is dictated by the sign of its derivative, yielding uniform bounds for integrable ones, and mild local decay along the KdV soliton. We also find a monotone horizon-localized norm, which is not of Aretakis type, showing that stability properties are directly sensitive to the near-horizon structure encoded in the Schwarzian background. We compute the associated Regge--Teitelboim charges at a late-time corner of the throat using a radial ADM foliation of the spacetime.

title: The fate of hidden symmetries under magnetic Harrison transformations
summary: Solution-generating transformations construct new geometries from known seeds, raising the question of whether and to what extent the resulting solutions inherit the hidden symmetries underlying the seeds' integrability and separability. We have established universal perturbative inheritance laws for CKTs and massless scalar separability directly at the level of magnetic Harrison transformations, encompassing both magnetization of Carter-type seeds and demagnetization of conformal Carter-type seeds. In both magnetized Kerr and demagnetized Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson, this perturbative inheritance coexists with the loss of exact Carter-type separability, while seed-connected conformal Killing-Yano structures are already obstructed at the same perturbative order. These results reveal a hierarchy in the perturbative survival of hidden symmetries and provide a framework for investigating their inheritance in more general theoretical settings and under other solution-generating transformations.

title: Drift of a Charged Particle in a Black Hole Magnetosphere: the Effect of Black Hole Spin
summary: Sparse plasma immersed in a strong magnetic field is common in astrophysical scenarios, for which a collisionless description is more appropriate. The guiding-center approximation serves as an effective tool for describing the motion of charged particles in a strong magnetic field, revealing the drift, a sub-leading order motion that causes particles to deviate from the magnetic field lines. It is widely accepted that the charged particles drift under the induction of gravity in Newtonian framework. However, a covariant formulation of the guiding-center approximation, as well as the drift of a charged particle induced by strong gravitational field, has yet to be fully explored. As a preliminary study, we aim to analyze the drift of a single charged particle in a black hole magnetosphere via a covariant approach. Particularly, we focus on the effects of black hole spin. We first examine the drift caused by the rotation of a massive object in the Newtonian regime using the language of gravitoelectromagnetism. A covariant formula of drift is derived, which is confirmed to reduce to the Newtonian results in the weak gravitational field and low speed limit. The impact of BH spin on the drift is analyzed in detail in Kerr spacetime specifically, for which we define the drift rate whose value quantifies the significance of the drift. Our results indicate that the impact of BH spin on the drift of a charged particle in a BH magnetosphere can be comparable to that of other factors in some extreme cases.

title: Chaotic motion of spinning particles in nonlocal gravity
summary: We study spin-induced chaos around a static, spherically symmetric black hole in revised Deser--Woodard nonlocal gravity (NLG), using the conservative test-body approximation relevant to extreme-mass-ratio inspirals. The deformation parameter $\zeta$ describes departures from Schwarzschild spacetime. Poincaré sections, rotation curves, and fast Lyapunov indicators (FLIs) reveal changes in resonant structures and a decreasing fraction of non-plunging trajectories classified as chaotic within the sampled family, from $37.5\%$ at $\zeta=0$ to zero at $\zeta=0.1$. The FLI classifications of selected trajectories are reflected in their approximate mass-quadrupole waveforms: neighboring chaotic and regular trajectories show a marked local spectral-flatness contrast, which weakens in backgrounds where both are classified as regular. To assess whether a transition from chaotic to regular motion caused by the background deformation helps distinguish NLG from GR, we compare NLG waveforms at $\zeta=10^{-6}$ with GR waveforms generated at different initial radii. For a trajectory whose classification changes between the backgrounds, this adjustment substantially reduces the mismatch. The selected NLG waveforms from chaotic orbits retain larger minimum mismatches than those from regular orbits, although sensitivity to initial conditions may also hinder signal recovery. These results connect background-dependent orbital dynamics with radiation spectra, but do not establish that chaos offers an advantage for identifying the background geometry.

title: Numerical evidence for the validity of the inverse hoop conjecture for black holes
summary: The inverse hoop (IH) conjecture, ${\cal M}_{\text{irr}}\leq {\cal C}_{\text{s}}/4\pi$, originally discussed in the context of stationary black-hole configurations, suggests that the surface area of a black hole cannot undergo unconstrained geometric wrinkling (here ${\cal M}_{\text{irr}}=\sqrt{{\cal A}/16\pi}$ is the irreducible mass associated with the horizon area ${\cal A}$ of the black hole and ${\cal C}_{\text{s}}$ is the circumference length of the smallest ring that can engulf the horizon of the black hole in every direction). In the present compact paper we provide evidence supporting the validity of the IH conjecture for non-stationary black-hole configurations. In particular, we show that all the non-stationary black-hole solutions recently constructed by Croft, García-Moreno, and Pani (CGP) [arXiv:2611.13266] satisfy the IH relation.

title: Two-scale system: compactified ambient metrics and Scri/Spi/Ti
summary: We show that certain geometric constructions, including the Fefferman-Graham ambient metric, Brinkmann spaces, and ultrastatic vacuum spacetimes, admit natural conformal compactifications and can be unified within a single framework arising naturally from conformal geometry. The framework is based on a two-scale system comprising two weight-one conformal scalars satisfying almost-Einstein equations and certain regularity conditions. As a particular instance of this unifying framework, we obtain a new ambient construction for Spi and Ti, the extended spatial and temporal infinities of Ricci-flat spacetimes. A remarkable feature of this construction is that Spi/Ti and the null infinity of the corresponding spacetimes are naturally realised as a boundary face and the corner of the two-scale ambient space, respectively. We also demonstrate how the two-scale system can serve as a background ambient geometry for studying the asymptotic behaviour of (gauge) fields at spatial, temporal, and null infinity.

title: A Stable Vector Bounce
summary: We construct a geodesically complete bounce in cubic generalised Proca theory with a free canonical scalar as the matter field. The temporal vector evolves along its algebraic constraint and supports the transition from contraction to expansion while matter obeys the null energy condition. This evolution permits nonzero derivative mixing at the bounce. The kinetic coefficients are positive at every finite time for all nonzero comoving wavenumbers, and short-wavelength perturbations are stable throughout the solution. Following the linear equations to both infinite-time limits also shows that local perturbations are bounded for all nonzero comoving wavenumbers.

title: Black holes in Myrzakulov $F(R,T)$ gravity
summary: We investigate vacuum black-hole solutions in metric-affine Myrzakulov $F(R,T)$ gravity (MG-I), where $R$ is the affine Ricci scalar and $T$ is a quadratic torsion invariant, not the trace of the matter energy-momentum tensor. For the polynomial model $F(R,T)=\alpha R+\beta T+\gamma T^3$, with $\alpha\neq0$, we first vary the metric and all components of the independent affine connection, and only then specialize to metric-compatible geometry with totally antisymmetric torsion. Nonzero axial torsion admits an exceptional branch $\alpha+\beta+3\gamma T_*^2=0$, on which the metric satisfies the Einstein equations with effective cosmological parameter $\Lambda_*=\gamma T_*^3/\alpha$. We establish a local existence result and construct torsionful Schwarzschild-(anti-)de Sitter representatives that are smooth through a selected future Killing horizon. Within the spherically symmetric axial ansatz, we characterize Ricci-symmetric affine connections by the condition $(fV-U)'=0$ and compare a constant-$W=fV-U$ family with a constant-$U$ family. Although these connections share the same metric and torsion scalar, their affine curvature invariants generally differ. Independent coordinate-level curvature contractions and component tests of the unrestricted metric and connection variations corroborate the identities used in the construction; these checks complement the analytic variational derivation. Finally, we identify null directions of the restricted axial quadratic form and distinguish this degeneracy from a complete metric-affine stability analysis. Our conclusions are local and do not establish global extendibility, physical inequivalence of all torsion profiles, or dynamical stability.

title: Relativistic precession around rotating neutron stars. I. Slow rotation: Hartle--Thorne spacetimes, particle orbits and the QPOs of atoll and Z sources
summary: We study the relativistic precession model (RPM) of quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the spacetimes of slowly rotating neutron stars computed from the equation of state (EOS). For four EOSs (WFF1, G3, FSUGarnet and IOPB-I) we solve the Hartle--Thorne equations to second order in the angular velocity and compute the orbital and epicyclic frequencies of the exterior metric without expanding in the spin or the quadrupole. At $1.9\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ the spin-induced quadrupole is 2--4 times that of a black hole with the same spin; it lowers the nodal precession frequency by up to 25 per cent near the innermost stable circular orbit and limits the nodal frequency that any spin can produce. An eccentric, tilted geodesic around a $1.92\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ star spinning at 363~Hz precesses at the epicyclic rates, and the power spectrum of a hot spot on it peaks at the orbital, periastron and nodal precession frequencies. Applied to the atoll sources 4U 1636$-$53 and 4U 1728$-$34, the RPM gives masses of 2.02--$2.15\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ and 1.88--$1.92\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$. For 4U 1728$-$34 the low-frequency QPO favours stars with large moments of inertia, $I\simeq2.5\times10^{45}$~g\,cm$^{2}$. Without an EOS the QPOs give $M=1.920^{+0.014}_{-0.012}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$, $j=0.162^{+0.023}_{-0.011}$ and $\bar Q=2.2^{+1.1}_{-0.8}$; a Kerr spacetime with the same nodal frequency would underestimate the moment of inertia by 22 per cent. For the Z sources GX 5$-$1 and GX 340+0 the horizontal-branch oscillations cannot be twice the nodal precession frequency for any of the four EOSs: the fits are driven to spins of 730--745~Hz and to the maximum mass.

title: Scalar charge of neutron stars and accreting black holes in Starobinsky gravity: quasi-universal relations, the trace anomaly and gravitational-wave sensitivity
summary: The Starobinsky scalaron is sourced by the trace of the stress--energy, so its exterior charge is set by the matter around an object and not by the object's vacuum geometry. We derive a master formula for that charge for any static, spherically symmetric source, evaluate it first for neutron stars, where the interior is known, and then for accreting black holes, where it is not. For a star the pressure subtracts: on the interior metric with the Eardley sensitivity, and the charge is a quasi-universal function of the compactness. Six realistic equations of state confirm the relation but lie above the coefficient calibrated on polytropes; the refit reproduces their mean to 0.007. The trace $\rho-3p$ changes sign in the cores of massive stars, and the charge also tracks the tidal deformability and the moment of inertia to a few parts in 1000 and 100. Solving the Einstein-frame structure equations self-consistently moves a star along this relation and leaves its charge at fixed compactness within 4 per cent of the test-field value. We compare the charge with NICER radii and the GW170817 tidal deformability, and use the published massless dipole constraint from GW230529 to calibrate a Fisher estimate of the sensitivity of a similar binary to a finite scalaron range, projected to the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer; the range is a free parameter, and the laboratory bound on pure $R+\alpha R^2$ is confronted explicitly. A vacuum black hole has q=0; a hole with a disc has $q=\sinh(m_\phi r_d)/(m_\phi r_d)$, controlled by the disc's outer edge, which makes it the counterpart in which the same integral is dominated by matter far from the centre; light is blind to the charge at leading order, and the correction beyond it is negligible for any self-consistent disc.

title: Dymnikova black string
summary: We obtain a new static black string solution of Einstein's equations with a negative cosmological constant sourced by a Dymnikova-type anisotropic matter distribution. At large radial distances, the geometry approaches the Lemos black string, while the behavior near the central region is characterized by an effective curvature parameter. We examine the weak and strong energy conditions, the horizon structure, and the curvature invariants. The Ricci and Kretschmann scalars remain finite at the origin. We also investigate the Hawking temperature and heat capacity, with particular attention to the dependence of the thermodynamic behavior on the Dymnikova scale.

title: Multi-throat generalized Ellis--Bronnikov wormholes with asymptotic string-cloud behavior
summary: We study an ultrastatic, spherically symmetric family of traversable wormholes obtained by locally deforming a generalized Ellis--Bronnikov areal-radius profile in a spacetime with an asymptotic angular deficit. Depending on the deformation parameters, the same analytic family contains one, two, three, or four throats. The corresponding bifurcation curves are obtained in dimensionless form, and the resulting geometries are regular and asymptotically conical.
